exercise.name: Iso-Lateral High Row
library_steps: Sit with your thighs under the pad and reach up to the high handles.
Pull the handles down and back toward your chest.
Let them rise slowly until your arms are straight.
exercise.one_line_summary: Seated with the thighs under pads, neutral handles high in front. Picture 1: arms reaching up and forward; picture 2: handles pulled down and back to the chest, elbows by the sides.

muscles.emg: Downward-and-back pull = shoulder extension/adduction, the latissimus action (S1, S2).
muscles.surface: Side and lower back, under the armpit.

muscles.emg: Trapezius/rhomboids retract the shoulder blades at the end (S1).

mistakes.why_it_matters: Keep the trunk still, move the arms (S1).

sources.citation: Lehman GJ, Buchan DD, Lundy A, Myers N, Nalborczyk A. Variations in muscle activation levels during traditional latissimus dorsi weight training exercises: an experimental study. Dyn Med. 2004;3(1):4.
sources.what_it_gave: Seated row gave the highest middle trapezius/rhomboid activity; wide-grip pulldown and seated row had the best lat-to-biceps ratio.

sources.citation: Lusk SJ, Hale BD, Russell DM. Grip width and forearm orientation effects on muscle activity during the lat pull-down. J Strength Cond Res. 2010;24(7):1895-1900.
sources.what_it_gave: Lat pulldown: a pronated grip gave greater latissimus dorsi activity than a supinated grip; grip width mattered less.

sources.citation: Padovan R, Ce E, Longo S, Tornatore G, Esposito F, Coratella G. High-density surface electromyography excitation of prime movers across scapular positions in the seated row. J Funct Morphol Kinesiol. 2025;11(1):6.
sources.what_it_gave: Seated row HD-EMG: latissimus, trapezius and posterior deltoid excitation across shoulder-blade positions.

clip_check.target: 145 deg, up and forward -> 50 deg, elbows down and back (within 10 deg)

clip_check.check: Machine parts meet the hands/feet; levers keep their length
clip_check.target: moving rod lengths equal at start and end (+-1 cm)
